section: Closing strips and fillers for Maxima and Intarsio
source_pages: printed p.434 / PDF 436 (subset extracted: the H.210 row of the first position)

filler_front.description: Filler in door finishes from 2,3 to 15 cm - front in door finishes

front_layout.note: One finished front covering the whole face. NO hinge_axis and no mechanism - A FILLER DOES NOT OPEN, so 70_symbols draws no leaf, which is the same treatment a US appliance panel gets: it too states a single front it never swings. The kind is STATED rather than left absent because Panel.effective_slabs and Panel.gola_options both default a missing layout to 'single', and a default is not a source. THIS FAMILY HAS NO DOOR-VERSION AXIS: tall_h210.json declares door_versions null and the element is 2100 mm tall, so 78/75 means nothing here and nothing about this front changes with a gola run. Until 2026-08-24 this note ended with a sentence copied from fillers_h78.json which claimed the front changed height in the gola version, quoting family H.78's own gola door height. It was an H.78 fact, it was wrong here, and it contradicted base_h78.json, which states in its own door_versions note that the axis is family-scoped. Corrected in place 2026-08-24; the mistake and how it surfaced are kept in claude/findings-2026-08-24-filler-note.md. AND IT WOULD HAVE GOT WORSE, NOT BETTER: the section 'Tall units H. 210 | for base unit H. 78' (printed p.116-125, letters C5 d.35 / C6 d.62) DOES print 78 and 75 - as 132 + 78 and 132 + 75 - but only for its LOWER door. What a full-height 2100 filler does beside such a run is printed nowhere, so it is an open question and not a number to derive.

filler_front.not_buildable_reason: No depth is printed for this position - see fillers_h78.json, same article family, same reason.
filler_front.notes: CQ is the H.210 letter the tall chapter uses, and code_grammar.tall_units records that every tall section prints a PAIR - the first member d.35, the second d.62. This table prints only first members (CE, CQ, CG, C0 and never CF, CR, CH, C9), which is consistent with a front strip having no depth to choose. AN OBSERVATION, NOT A RULE, and one row already breaks it: CH9151 at H.278 uses a d.62 letter that the tall chapter assigns to H.222, and carries the only suffix on the page that is neither 0150 nor 0151. A family letter can be page-scoped exactly as a depth letter can. H.278 appears nowhere else in anything we have read.
